description: The four PDR fault types, exactly. Each fault perturbs ONE physical parameter in the generator; the multi-channel signature follows from the physics in DECISIONS.md section 4. Fault progress p goes from 0 at injection to 1 at true failure.
progress_rule: p(t) = 0 before inject_at_s; p(t) = ((t - inject_at_s) / time_to_failure_s) ** exponent while running; the component is FAILED when p reaches 1. parameter_value(p) = healthy_value + p * (at_failure - healthy_value).
calibration_rule: at_failure is chosen so that, at p = 1, the fault's primary channel sits at its CRITICAL limit in TRAVERSE_EMPTY at thermal steady state. Values below were hand-computed from the section 4 equations; the generator tests must confirm them.

signature_vocabulary.EXPLAINED_BY_CURRENT: raw value rises, but only by the amount the measured current predicts (residual stays near zero)

derived_signals.thermal_residual: measured drive temperature minus temperature predicted from measured current and speed by the detector's thermal model (positive = unexplained heat)
derived_signals.voltage_residual: measured battery voltage minus V_oc(SOC) - I * R_nominal (negative = extra sag)

faults.label: Wheel hub bearing wear
faults.mechanism: Worn or regolith-contaminated hub bearing adds friction torque. The motor draws more current to overcome it, the wheel slows, and the friction itself heats the hub directly.
faults.distinguish_from: wheel_drag: same current and speed pattern, but bearing_wear has a large positive thermal_residual because friction heat lands in the hub.

recommended_action.text: Stop driving as soon as safe. Go to P5. Replace hub bearing on the affected wheel; inspect seals and gearbox for regolith ingress.

candidate_sources: NASA Prognostics Center of Excellence data repository: IMS (Univ. of Cincinnati) bearing run-to-failure set - shape of the degradation curve
Case Western Reserve University Bearing Data Center - kHz vibration with seeded faults; useful only if a vibration channel is added, not for 1 Hz current/temperature trends

faults.label: Wheel drag in regolith
faults.mechanism: Regolith packing into the wheel well and tread adds rolling resistance. The extra work goes into shearing soil outside the hub, so the hub only warms from the extra I^2 R copper loss.
faults.distinguish_from: bearing_wear: same current and speed pattern, but thermal_residual stays near zero. Raw temperature may still rise a little (about +12 degC at failure in TRAVERSE_EMPTY) because copper loss grows with I^2.

recommended_action.text: Reduce speed and payload. At P5, clear regolith from the wheel well, tread and seals; inspect the tread for damage.

candidate_sources: No public run-to-failure dataset identified. Terramechanics literature could bound rolling-resistance values - still to be found and cited.

faults.label: Thermal / cooling fault
faults.mechanism: Dust coating the radiator or a degraded thermal strap raises the drive's thermal resistance to its heat sink. Same heat in, worse heat out, so temperature climbs while current stays normal.
faults.distinguish_from: bearing_wear: both have positive thermal_residual, but cooling_fault has normal current and speed.

recommended_action.text: Limit drive duty cycle. At P5, clean the radiator surface and inspect the thermal strap / heat pipe on the affected drive.

candidate_sources: No public dataset identified. Lunar dust-on-radiator studies could bound the degradation rate - still to be found and cited.

faults.label: Battery degradation
faults.mechanism: Internal resistance of the pack rises with ageing. Terminal voltage sags further under load (sag = I * R_int), and the sag worsens over time.
faults.distinguish_from: Low SOC: a flat battery has low voltage but a normal residual. Degradation shows as a residual that grows with load current.

recommended_action.text: Limit peak load and keep SOC high. At P5, run an impedance test and replace the weak module or the pack.

candidate_sources: NASA Prognostics Center of Excellence data repository: Li-ion battery ageing set (18650 cells cycled with impedance measurements) - growth of internal resistance over life
